extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry; instructors and self-learners working through Chapter 2 exercises and commentary
extracted.subtask_description: Worked solutions, corrections and explanatory remarks for Chapter 2 of a commutative algebra textbook (module theory, tensor products, flatness, direct limits, algebraic varieties). Contains statements, proof sketches, corrections to imprecise formulations, and exercise hints. Useful for learners solving and checking exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show µ : X → Max(C(X)) is a homeomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove the map µ sending x to mx (functions vanishing at x) is a homeomorphism of a compact Hausdorff space X onto Max(C(X)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove three parts: (i) surjectivity: for any maximal ideal m, its common zero set V(m) is non-empty (compactness used to show a finite sum of squares would otherwise be a unit in m), hence m = mx for some x; (ii) injectivity: continuous functions separate points (Urysohn's lemma), so distinct points give distinct maximal ideals; (iii) topology: show µ(Uf) = {m | f ∉ m} for basic open sets Uf = {x | f(x) ≠ 0}; Uf (resp. those sets) form a basis, so µ is a homeomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate ring ↔ Max(P(X)) bijection (affine variety)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an affine algebraic variety X over an algebraically closed field k, the map µ : X → Max(P(X)) sending x to mx is injective; surjectivity is equivalent to Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Injectivity: if x ≠ y then some coordinate function ξi separates coordinates, so mx ≠ my. Surjectivity requires Nullstellensatz (stated as 'less obvious (but still true)').

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular maps ↔ k-algebra homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: A map φ : X → Y between affine varieties is regular iff it is the restriction of a polynomial map kn → km; such a φ induces a k-algebra homomorphism P(Y) → P(X) by η ↦ η ◦ φ, and this gives a one-to-one correspondence between regular maps X → Y and k-algebra homomorphisms P(Y) → P(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: to φ associate ψ(g) := g ◦ φ; conversely from ψ construct φ by evaluating images of coordinate functions; show ψ(I(Y)) ⊆ I(X) and conversely if ψ maps I(Y) into I(X) then φ maps X into Y. Use the identity g(ψ(u1)(x),...,ψ(um)(x)) = ψ(g)(x) (display (11)) to check the constructions are inverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct formulation of Proposition 2.4 (endomorphism equation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated A-module, a an ideal of A, and φ an A-module endomorphism with φ(M) ⊆ aM, then φ satisfies an equation of the form φ^n + ψ(a1) φ^{n−1} + ··· + ψ(an) = 0 where ψ : A → End_A(M) is the natural morphism and ai ∈ a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mix elements of A with endomorphisms: either apply the natural map ψ to scalars or equip End_A(M) with its A-module structure and write φ^n + a1 φ^{n−1} + ··· + an φ^0 = 0. If φ = ψ(y) for y ∈ A then ψ(y^n + a1 y^{n−1} + ··· + an)=0 (equation (12)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: matrix adjoint/determinant proof for Prop 2.4
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove the corrected Proposition 2.4 use generators x1,...,xn of M, write φ(xi) as ∑ aij xj with aij ∈ a, form the matrix bij := δij φ − ψ(aij) in the commutative subring B of End_A(M) generated by ψ(A) and φ, take the adjoint (cij) and determinant det(bij) and conclude det(bij) annihilates the generators, yielding the desired polynomial relation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a constructive way to produce the annihilating polynomial with coefficients in a by expanding the determinant in End_A(M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deriving corollaries from Prop 2.4 (Nakayama-type consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the endomorphism equation one obtains: if aM = M with a ideal of A then there exists x ≡ 1 (mod a) with xM = 0; in particular, for a single element a with aM = M there exists b such that abm = m = bam for all m ∈ M; surjective endomorphisms of finitely generated modules are bijective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set φ = identity and apply the equation (12) with y = 1 to produce x = 1 + a1 + ... + an. Use polynomial-in-x tricks and Corollary 12/13 reasoning (e.g., view M as A[x]-module with x acting by φ) to deduce bijectivity of surjective endomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nakayama’s Lemma statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a finitely generated A-module and a an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of A, then aM = M implies M = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a central criterion for detecting triviality of finitely generated modules when a 'small' ideal acts surjectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing tensors lemma (finite support relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a ring, M a right A-module, N a left A-module, (yi) generating family of N, (xi) finitely supported in M and ∑ xi ⊗ yi = 0 in M ⊗_A N, then there exists a finite set J, elements x'_j ∈ M and finitely-supported aij ∈ A with x_i = ∑_j x'_j aij for all i and ∑_i aij yi = 0 for all j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the presentation of N as quotient of a free module and exactness of tensoring; this lemma is the standard way to convert a vanishing tensor into finite linear relations on generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted ideal criterion via tensor product
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring map A → B, an ideal a of A is contracted (a = f^{-1}(aB)) iff the natural map A/a → B ⊗_A A/a is injective. In particular, if a is proper and contracted then B ⊗_A A/a ≠ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute B ⊗_A A/a ≅ B / a_e (extension ideal) and observe Ker(A/a → B ⊗_A A/a) ≅ a_e c / a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct A→D homomorphism when tensoring algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: When forming tensor product B ⊗_A C of A-algebras and maps f : A→B, g : A→C, the correct embedding A → B ⊗_A C sends a to f(a) ⊗ 1 (equivalently 1 ⊗ g(a)), not to f(a) ⊗ g(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The map a ↦ f(a)⊗g(a) is incorrect; ensure scalars act via f(a)⊗1 = 1⊗g(a) when defining the canonical A-algebra structure on the tensor product. The tensor product is the coproduct in the category of A-algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation: (A/a) ⊗_A (A/b) ≅ A/(a + b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ideals a,b of A, A/a ⊗_A A/b is isomorphic to A/(a + b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Exercise 2.2 and standard tensor algebra to show A/a ⊗_A A/b ≅ (A/b) / a(A/b) ≅ A/(a + b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation: (A/a) ⊗_A M ≅ M / aM
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-module M and ideal a, the tensor (A/a) ⊗_A M is canonically isomorphic to M/aM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit unique A-linear map f : (A/a) ⊗ M → M/aM given by f(ā ⊗ x) = ax (mod aM); show exactness of a ⊗ M → M → (A/a)⊗ M → 0 and identify image of g with aM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local ring tensor-vanishing criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a local ring and M,N are finitely generated A-modules with M ⊗_A N = 0, then M = 0 or N = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use residue field k = A/m, reduction Mk = M/mM ≅ k ⊗_A M, apply Nakayama's lemma; M⊗N = 0 ⇒ (M⊗N)⊗_A k = Mk ⊗_k Nk = 0, so one of Mk or Nk is 0, then Nakayama gives trivial module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness preserved by direct sums and by polynomial extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct sum M = ⊕ Mi is flat iff each Mi is flat; in particular A[x] is flat as an A-algebra because as an A-module it is a direct sum of copies of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use decomposition of modules and universal property of tensor products; A[x] ≅ ⊕_{i≥0} A as A-modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial module identification: M[x] ≅ A[x] ⊗_A M
rubrics_metrics.description: For any A-module M, the module of polynomials with coefficients in M, M[x], is isomorphic to A[x] ⊗_A M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define bilinear map and check universal property to produce the isomorphism; left to reader in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime ideals extend to polynomial ring: p[x] prime, maximal may fail
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is prime in A then p[x] is prime in A[x]; if m is maximal in A, m[x] need not be maximal in A[x] (e.g., A a field, (0) maximal in A but (0) not maximal in A[x]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use isomorphism A[x]/p[x] ≅ (A/p)[x] to deduce primality; maximality fails because polynomial rings over fields are not fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of flat modules is flat; base change preserves flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) If M and N are flat A-modules then M ⊗_A N is flat. (ii) If B is flat over A and N is flat over B then N is flat over A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use associativity of tensor and exactness properties: (M ⊗ N) ⊗ P ≅ M ⊗ (N ⊗ P). For (ii) use N ⊗_A P ≅ N ⊗_B (B ⊗_A P).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation closed under short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0 is exact and M' and M'' are finitely generated, then M is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lift generators of M'' to M and combine with generators of M' to get generators of M (standard argument given in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surjectivity lifts from modulo ideal when ideal in Jacobson radical
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a be an ideal in the Jacobson radical of A. If u : M → N is a homomorphism with N finitely generated and the induced map M/aM → N/aN is surjective then u is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use N = aN + u(M) and Nakayama-type Corollary 2.7 to deduce N = u(M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank criterion: Am ≅ An implies m = n
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ≠ 0 and Am ≅ An as A-modules then m = n (finite free rank is invariant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize at a maximal ideal m and reduce to vector-space dimension over field A/m to compare ranks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel of surjection to free module finitely generated
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ : M → A^n is surjective and M is finitely generated, then Ker(φ) is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose preimages ui of standard basis elements generating a complement N; then M = Ker(φ) ⊕ N so Ker(φ) is a direct summand of a finitely generated module and hence finitely generated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction and extension of scalars: N → B ⊗_A N injective and split
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring homomorphism f : A → B and B-module N, regarding N as A-module by restriction, the natural map g : N → NB = B ⊗_A N, y ↦ 1 ⊗ y is injective and g(N) is a direct summand of NB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define p : NB → N by p(b ⊗ y) = by; then p ∘ g = id_N, so NB = Im(g) ⊕ Ker(p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit/colimit construction recipes (sets, modules, rings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits can be constructed as subobjects of products (equalizers) and colimits as quotients of coproducts (coequalizers); direct limits (inductive limits) of modules are constructed as (⊕ Mi)/relations generated by xi − µij(xi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipe: form coproduct C = ⊕ Mi and quotient by D generated by xi − µij(xi) (i ≤ j) to get M = C/D; verify universal property. For filtered (directed) systems, this yields the usual direct limit with elements represented by µi(xi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct limit element and zero-lifting properties
rubrics_metrics.description: In a direct limit M = lim→ Mi every element of M is µi(xi) for some i and xi ∈ Mi; if µi(xi) = 0 there exists j ≥ i with µij(xi) = 0 in Mj.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the defining properties of the direct limit used in checking universal properties and exactness arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor commutes with direct limits (colimits)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a directed system (Mi) and any A-module N, the natural map lim→ (Mi ⊗ N) → (lim→ Mi) ⊗ N is an isomorphism; equivalently, tensor product commutes with colimits (in particular with direct sums).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to showing M ⊗ (⨁ Ni) ≅ ⨁ (M ⊗ Ni) using explicit canonical maps f and inverse g (constructed by x ⊗ y ↦ family of x ⊗ y in the appropriate summand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct limit of rings inherits ring structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The direct limit A = lim→ Ai of a directed system of rings Ai inherits a ring structure making the canonical maps Ai → A ring homomorphisms; if A = 0 then some Ai = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat each Ai as Z-module to form the direct limit, then define multiplication compatibly via images from finite stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nilradical commutes with direct limits; domains preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: If Ni is the nilradical of Ai then lim→ Ni is the nilradical of lim→ Ai. If each Ai is an integral domain, then lim→ Ai is an integral domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from the universal property of direct limits and Exercise 2.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of family of A-algebras as coproduct
rubrics_metrics.description: For a family (Bλ)λ∈Λ of A-algebras, their tensor product over A (constructed as direct limit of tensor products over finite subsets) is the coproduct in the category of A-algebras; arbitrary coproducts exist and are given by these tensor constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct BJ = ⊗_{λ∈J} Bλ for finite J and take direct limit over finite J; note consequence that the category of A-algebras has all limits and colimits (products, equalizers, tensor-coproducts, coequalizers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness equivalent to vanishing Tor
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-module M, the following are equivalent: (i) M is flat; (ii) Tor^A_n(M,N) = 0 for all n > 0 and all N; (iii) Tor^A_1(M,N) = 0 for all N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: (i)⇒(ii) by tensoring a free resolution; (iii)⇒(i) by applying Tor exact sequence to short exact sequences 0→N'→N→N''→0 and checking M⊗ preserves exactness when Tor_1 vanishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake-lemma style arguments and lemma technicalities
rubrics_metrics.description: When dealing with commutative diagrams with exact rows (diagram (15),(16)), use lemmas about intersections and kernels/images (Lemmas 20–23) to build connecting maps between kernels and cokernels and deduce exactness properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical steps: show Im(β)∩Im(ū) = Im(ū◦α) when γ injective; Ker(β)+Im(u) = Ker(v̄◦β) when α surjective; extend to sequences on kernels and cokernels and check exactness under injectivity/surjectivity hypotheses. These technical tools underpin long exact sequences in homological algebra and arguments without Tor.
